35	/**
36	 * Destination picker dialog for intra-share file moves.
37	 *
38	 * Loads the full shared subtree via enumerateSharedSubtree on open. Disables
39	 * read-only folders (writable === false) and the current folder so the
40	 * recipient cannot select invalid destinations. The caller owns the move call
41	 * (moveItemHandler) and the post-move state refresh (sharedFolder:updated
42	 * projection — this component reads nothing back).
43	 */
44	export function SharedMoveDialog({
45	  open,
46	  onClose,
47	  onConfirm,
48	  item,
49	  items,
50	  currentFolderId,
51	  shareId,
52	  isLoading = false,
53	}: SharedMoveDialogProps) {
54	  // Batch mode when items prop is provided with more than one item
55	  const isBatchMode = Array.isArray(items) && items.length > 1;
56	  const [pickerNodes, setPickerNodes] = useState<SharedPickerNode[]>([]);
57	  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null);
58	  const [loadError, setLoadError] = useState<string | null>(null);
59	  const [isLoadingTree, setIsLoadingTree] = useState(false);
60	
61	  // Ref for async-ref safety: re-check after each await
62	  const openRef = useRef(open);
63	  openRef.current = open;
64	
65	  // Load the shared subtree when the dialog opens
66	  useEffect(() => {
67	    if (!open || !shareId) return;
68	    const auth = useAuthStore.getState();
69	    if (!auth.vaultKeypair) return;
70	
71	    setIsLoadingTree(true);
72	    setLoadError(null);
73	    setPickerNodes([]);
74	    setSelectedId(null);
75	
76	    getSdkClient()
77	      .enumerateSharedSubtree(shareId, {
78	        getShareKeysFn: fetchShareKeys,
79	        vaultPrivateKey: auth.vaultKeypair.privateKey,
80	      })
81	      .then((nodes) => {
82	        // Re-check after await: dialog may have been closed
83	        if (!openRef.current) return;
84	        setPickerNodes(nodes);
85	      })
86	      .catch(() => {
87	        if (!openRef.current) return;
88	        setLoadError('Failed to load folder tree');
89	      })
90	      .finally(() => {
91	        if (!openRef.current) return;
92	        setIsLoadingTree(false);
93	      });
94	  }, [open, shareId]);
95	
96	  // Reset state when dialog closes
97	  useEffect(() => {
98	    if (!open) {
99	      setSelectedId(null);
100	      setLoadError(null);
101	      setPickerNodes([]);
102	    }
103	  }, [open]);
104	
105	  const handleSelectNode = useCallback(
106	    (node: SharedPickerNode) => {
107	      const isDisabled = !node.writable || node.id === currentFolderId;
108	      if (isDisabled) return;
109	      setSelectedId(node.id);
110	    },
111	    [currentFolderId]
112	  );
113	
114	  const handleKeyDown = useCallback(
115	    (e: KeyboardEvent, node: SharedPickerNode) => {
116	      if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
117	        e.preventDefault();
118	        handleSelectNode(node);
119	      }
120	    },
121	    [handleSelectNode]
122	  );
123	
124	  const handleConfirm = useCallback(() => {
125	    if (!selectedId) return;
126	    const node = pickerNodes.find((n) => n.id === selectedId);
127	    if (!node) return;
128	    onConfirm(node.id, node.ipnsName);
129	  }, [selectedId, pickerNodes, onConfirm]);
130	
131	  const handleCancel = useCallback(() => {
132	    if (!isLoading) {
133	      onClose();
134	    }
135	  }, [isLoading, onClose]);
136	
137	  // Auto-adapt title/label for batch vs single mode (mirrors private MoveDialog :174-179)
138	  const title = isBatchMode
139	    ? `Move ${items!.length} items`
140	    : item?.type === 'folder'
141	      ? 'Move Folder'
142	      : 'Move File';
143	  const label = isBatchMode
144	    ? `Move ${items!.length} items to:`
145	    : item
146	      ? `Move "${item.name}" to:`
147	      : 'Move to:';
148	
149	  const selectedNode = pickerNodes.find((n) => n.id === selectedId);
150	  const isValid = !!selectedNode && selectedNode.writable && selectedNode.id !== currentFolderId;
151	
152	  return (
153	    <Modal open={open} onClose={handleCancel} title={title}>
154	      <div className="dialog-content">
155	        <div className="dialog-field">
156	          <label className="dialog-label">{label}</label>
157	
158	          {isLoadingTree && (
159	            <div className="move-dialog-empty">{'// loading shared folders...'}</div>
160	          )}
161	
162	          {loadError && <span className="dialog-error">{loadError}</span>}
163	
164	          {!isLoadingTree && !loadError && (
165	            <div
166	              className="move-dialog-folder-list"
167	              role="listbox"
168	              aria-label="Select destination folder"
169	            >
170	              {pickerNodes.length === 0 && (
171	                <div className="move-dialog-empty">No writable folders available</div>
172	              )}
173	              {pickerNodes.map((node) => {
174	                const isDisabled = !node.writable || node.id === currentFolderId;
175	                const isSelected = selectedId === node.id;
176	                const disabledReason = !node.writable
177	                  ? 'Read-only folder'
178	                  : node.id === currentFolderId
179	                    ? 'Item is already here'
180	                    : undefined;
181	
182	                return (
183	                  <div
184	                    key={node.id}
185	                    className={[
186	                      'move-dialog-folder-item',
187	                      'shared-move-dialog-folder-item',
188	                      isSelected ? 'move-dialog-folder-item--selected' : '',
189	                      isDisabled ? 'move-dialog-folder-item--disabled' : '',
190	                    ]
191	                      .filter(Boolean)
192	                      .join(' ')}
193	                    role="button"
194	                    tabIndex={isDisabled ? -1 : 0}
195	                    aria-disabled={isDisabled}
196	                    aria-pressed={isSelected}
197	                    title={disabledReason}
198	                    onClick={() => handleSelectNode(node)}
199	                    onKeyDown={(e) => handleKeyDown(e, node)}
200	                  >
201	                    <span className="move-dialog-folder-icon">[DIR]</span>
202	                    <span className="move-dialog-folder-name">{node.name}</span>
203	                    {!node.writable && (
204	                      <span className="shared-move-dialog-readonly-badge">{'[RO]'}</span>
205	                    )}
206	                  </div>
207	                );
208	              })}
209	            </div>
210	          )}
211	        </div>
212	
213	        <div className="dialog-actions">
214	          <button
215	            type="button"
216	            className="dialog-button dialog-button--secondary"
217	            onClick={handleCancel}
218	            disabled={isLoading}
219	          >
220	            Cancel
221	          </button>
222	          <button
223	            type="button"
224	            className="dialog-button dialog-button--primary"
225	            onClick={handleConfirm}
226	            disabled={isLoading || !isValid}
227	          >
228	            {isLoading ? 'Moving...' : 'Move'}
229	          </button>
230	        </div>
231	      </div>
232	    </Modal>
233	  );
234	}

1	/**
2	 * useSharedWriteOps -- Write operation handlers for shared folders.
3	 *
4	 * Handles upload, create folder, rename, update, and delete within shared
5	 * folders. Every handler routes through the SDK client's shared-folder methods
6	 * (`getSdkClient().<method>(currentShareId, args)`) and reads NOTHING back
7	 * (REQ-3, phase 48): the SDK owns publish + sequence + CAS retry. The
8	 * `folderChildrenRef`/`sequenceNumberRef` projections are fed solely by the
9	 * `sharedFolder:updated` subscription in `useSharedNavigation` — never written
10	 * here. This mirrors the Phase-47 owned-path consolidation
11	 * (useFileOperations/useFileVersions).
12	 */
13	
14	import { useCallback } from 'react';
15	import type { FolderChild, FilePointer } from '@cipherbox/core';
16	import { unwrapKey, hexToBytes } from '@cipherbox/crypto';
17	import { withRevocationGuard as sdkWithRevocationGuard } from '@cipherbox/sdk';
18	import { useAuthStore } from '../stores/auth.store';
19	import { fetchShareKeys } from '../services/share.service';
20	import { getSdkClient } from '../lib/sdk-provider';
21	import { logger } from '../lib/logger';
22	import type { SharedListItem } from './useSharedNavigation';
23	
24	export type SharedWriteOpsParams = {
25	  currentShareId: string | null;
26	  sharedItems: SharedListItem[];
27	  setIsLoading: (loading: boolean) => void;
28	  setError: (error: string | null) => void;
29	  handleRevocation: (silent: boolean) => void;
30	};
31	
32	export function useSharedWriteOps(p: SharedWriteOpsParams) {
33	  /**
34	   * Wrap a write operation with 403 revocation detection.
35	   * Orthogonal to CAS (which the SDK owns) — kept on the web side because the
36	   * revocation UX (zero key, flip to read-only) is web state.
37	   */
38	  const withRevocationGuard = useCallback(
39	    async <T>(operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> => {
40	      return sdkWithRevocationGuard(operation, () => p.handleRevocation(true));
41	    },
42	    [p.handleRevocation]
43	  );
44	
45	  /**
46	   * Run a folder write op through the SDK client. State updates (children /
47	   * sequence) arrive via the sharedFolder:updated subscription — nothing is read
48	   * back here.
49	   */
50	  const runWrite = useCallback(
51	    async (op: (shareId: string) => Promise<void>, failMessage: string): Promise<void> => {
52	      const shareId = p.currentShareId;
53	      if (!shareId) {
54	        p.setError('Write access not available');
55	        return;
56	      }
57	      p.setIsLoading(true);
58	      p.setError(null);
59	      try {
60	        await withRevocationGuard(() => op(shareId));
61	      } catch (err) {
62	        const message = (err as Error).message || failMessage;
63	        if (!message.includes('write access revoked')) {
64	          p.setError(message);
65	        }
66	        logger.error(`[SharedNav] ${failMessage}:`, err);
67	      } finally {
68	        p.setIsLoading(false);
69	      }
70	    },
71	    [p.currentShareId, p.setError, p.setIsLoading, withRevocationGuard]
72	  );
73	
74	  /**
75	   * Upload a file to the currently-viewed write-shared folder.
76	   */
77	  const uploadFileHandler = useCallback(
78	    async (file: File) => {
79	      await runWrite(async (shareId) => {
80	        const data = new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer());
81	        await getSdkClient().uploadToSharedFolder(shareId, {
82	          data,
83	          fileName: file.name,
84	          mimeType: file.type || undefined,
85	        });
86	      }, 'Shared folder upload failed');
87	    },
88	    [runWrite]
89	  );
90	
91	  /**
92	   * Create a subfolder in the currently-viewed write-shared folder.
93	   */
94	  const createFolderHandler = useCallback(
95	    async (name: string) => {
96	      await runWrite(async (shareId) => {
97	        await getSdkClient().createSharedSubfolder(shareId, { name });
98	      }, 'Shared folder create failed');
99	    },
100	    [runWrite]
101	  );
102	
103	  /**
104	   * Rename an item in the currently-viewed write-shared folder.
105	   */
106	  const renameItemHandler = useCallback(
107	    async (item: FolderChild, newName: string) => {
108	      await runWrite(async (shareId) => {
109	        await getSdkClient().renameInSharedFolder(shareId, { itemId: item.id, newName });
110	      }, 'Shared folder rename failed');
111	    },
112	    [runWrite]
113	  );
114	
115	  /**
116	   * Update a file's content in the currently-viewed write-shared folder.
117	   *
118	   * File-only publish: the SDK publishes the file's own IPNS metadata (folder
119	   * children/sequence unchanged) and emits sharedFolder:updated so the

```
## Security Review Complete — Phase 49 shared-folder move

Overall risk: **LOW**. Findings: CRITICAL 0 · HIGH 0 · MEDIUM 1 · LOW 3 · INFO 2.

The move path is solid. All six STRIDE threats verified: write-cap guard ordering is correct (dest `folder` + `folder-ipns` presence checked before any unwrap/publish), publish order is DEST → re-key → SOURCE with idempotent re-key, file IPNS keys come only from `share_keys file-ipns` (never owner-wrapped FilePointer), folderNav clones SDK buffers to avoid use-after-zero, and move-path key zeroing covers every throw path. No key material in any log or error.

### Top finding (the only actionable one)

**[MEDIUM] `enumerateSharedSubtree` leaks per-iteration folderKey — no zeroing**
`packages/sdk/src/client.ts:2460-2489`

Each DFS step unwraps a subfolder's AES-256 `folderKey` from `share_keys` (line 2460), uses it for `loadFolderMetadata` (2480), then drops the reference without `.fill(0)`. The move path zeroes everything in `finally`; this method does not. A deep share leaves one plaintext folder key per reachable subfolder live in heap, and if `loadFolderMetadata` throws mid-walk the in-flight key is abandoned too. Violates the project "clear key material after use" rule. Fix: wrap the per-iteration body in `try/finally` with `clearBytes(folderKey)` — `clearBytes`/`unwrapKey`/`hexToBytes` are already importable from `@cipherbox/crypto` (the import line is `client.ts:22`).

### LOW (non-blocking)
- Double-zero of `fileIpnsPrivateKey` (`client.ts:2389` ↔ `sdk-core/src/file/index.ts:372`) — benign/idempotent, just undocumented dual ownership.
- Batch move re-fetches share keys + re-unwraps per item (`useSharedWriteOps.ts:218-249`) — minor perf + benign TOCTOU, caught by the per-item guard + revocation guard.
- Re-key path discards `prunedCids` so the old source-key-sealed FileMetadata CID stays pinned (`reencrypt.ts:77-85`) — storage hygiene only (ciphertext), pre-existing shared-with-owner behavior.

Report: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.planning/security/REVIEW-phase49-20260618T025359Z.md`

Key source locations referenced: `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:2292-2495`, `packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts:529-594`, `packages/sdk/src/reencrypt.ts`, `packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts:369-372` (the upstream `fileIpnsPrivateKey` zeroing), `apps/web/src/hooks/useFolderNavigation.ts:264-265` (the buffer clones).

The report also lists six test-case suggestions not in the existing suites — the highest-value being an `enumerateSharedSubtree` test asserting every per-iteration `folderKey` is zeroed (which currently fails, proving the MEDIUM finding).

I now have everything needed. Both confirmations are in: the stateless `moveInSharedFolder` op (shared-write.ts) has zero descendant/cycle logic — only the `destFolderId === itemId` direct self-move check in client.ts:2306. The descendant guard lives purely in the dialog UI. And `moveItem` core op (sdk-core) does name-collision but no cycle check.

Here is my review.

## GENERAL SECURITY REVIEW — Phase 49 (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation)

**Overall risk: LOW**

Scope reviewed: SharedMoveDialog.tsx, SharedFolderRow.tsx, SharedFileBrowser.tsx, useSharedWriteOps.ts, shared-folder-projection.ts, useFolderNavigation.ts, client.ts (`moveInSharedFolder` + `enumerateSharedSubtree`), share/shared-write.ts. Crypto/key-handling deliberately excluded.

Findings: 0 critical, 0 high, 2 medium (both bounded-DoS / data-integrity, not exploitable for confidentiality), 3 low/defense-in-depth nits, 1 UX functional gap with a security-relevant failure mode.

---

### Lens 1 — Injection / XSS: CLEAN

- Folder/item names in `SharedMoveDialog.tsx:233` (`{node.name}`) and `SharedFolderRow.tsx` name cell render through React's text-interpolation sink — auto-escaped. No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no `innerHTML`, no direct DOM construction anywhere in the diff.
- The `title={disabledReason}` attribute (SharedMoveDialog.tsx:225) and `title={item.name}` patterns are attribute-bound, not HTML-parsed — safe.
- The drag `application/json` payload is parsed defensively at `SharedFolderRow.tsx` `handleDrop`: wrapped in try/catch, `Array.isArray(parsed.items)` + length-0 shape check, and parsed `id`s are used only as equality keys (`i.id === item.id`) and forwarded to `onMoveItemTo(item.id, ...)`. Notably the dropped payload's `id`s are *not* trusted — the handler routes by the *current selection state* (`selectedIds`/`selectedItems` in SharedFileBrowser), and the destination is `item.id` of the React-bound row, not anything from the payload. Even a forged payload can only trigger a move of items the user already has selected to a folder they can see. No eval, no DOM injection. Good.

### Lens 2 — Authorization / cycle guard: 1 MEDIUM (integrity, defense-in-depth gap)

### [MEDIUM] Descendant-cycle guard is UI-only; SDK op cannot detect a move into a descendant

**Location:** `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:2306-2309` (only `destFolderId === itemId` checked) and `packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts` `moveInSharedFolder` (no cycle logic); descendant guard lives only at `SharedMoveDialog.tsx:124-141` (`disabledDestIds`).

**Issue:** The dialog computes `disabledDestIds` by walking `enumerateSharedSubtree`'s `parentId` chain and disables the moved folder's whole subtree. But the SDK `moveInSharedFolder` only guards the direct self-move (`destFolderId === args.itemId`). The stateless op (`shareOps.moveInSharedFolder`) loads only *dest children* and *source children* — it never enumerates the moved folder's subtree, so it structurally *cannot* detect "dest is a descendant of the moved folder." A crafted client (or a future non-dialog caller) that calls `client.moveInSharedFolder(shareId, { itemId: folderA, destFolderId: folderA_child, ... })` would publish a folder-tree cycle.

**Impact:** Not a confidentiality/authz breach — the actor must already hold write keys (`folder-ipns` share_keys) for both source and dest, i.e. they could already corrupt their own writable subtree by other means. Worst case is **self-inflicted tree corruption / orphaned subtree** (folder A now references a child that references A), and the cycle could then make `enumerateSharedSubtree`'s `visited` set the only thing preventing an infinite walk for *other* recipients of the same share. So one writer can degrade the shared structure for co-recipients. This is an integrity/DoS-amplification gap, not a key-exposure gap.

**Recommendation:** Add a descendant check in `client.moveInSharedFolder` before publishing when `movedItem.type === 'folder'`: reuse `enumerateSharedSubtree` (or a lighter `parentId`-chain check against the already-loaded share tree) to assert `destFolderId` is not in the moved folder's subtree, throwing before any publish. This closes the bypass for non-UI callers and makes the guard authoritative rather than presentational. Mark the dialog guard as the UX layer and the SDK check as the enforcement layer.

### Lens 3 — DoS / resource exhaustion: 1 MEDIUM

### [MEDIUM] `enumerateSharedSubtree` and `batchMoveItems` are bounded only by share size — no explicit cap, sequential network amplification

**Location:** `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:2421-2480` (DFS) and `apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedWriteOps.ts` `batchMoveItemsHandler`.

**Issue (DFS):** The `visited` set keyed by `ipnsName` (client.ts:2436) is correct and prevents infinite recursion on a maliciously cyclic share structure — good. However the DFS does **one `loadFolderMetadata` network round-trip per folder node** and **one `unwrapKey` per node**, with no depth or node-count ceiling. A share owner who hands a recipient a deeply-nested or very-wide share (attacker controls the structure they shared) forces the recipient's client to do O(folders) sequential IPNS resolves on every dialog open. This runs on the main thread path of opening the move dialog.

**Issue (batch move):** `batchMoveItemsHandler` loops `moveInSharedFolder` per selected item sequentially; each call does its own `getShareKeysFn(shareId)` fetch (`client.ts:2316`) plus a dest `loadFolderMetadata` and 2 publishes. So N selected items = N share-key fetches + N dest-metadata loads + 2N publishes. Selection is user-driven (bounded by what's rendered), so this is lower risk, but the per-item re-fetch of the *same* `share_keys` is pure amplification.

**Impact:** Client-side latency/CPU/network amplification only — no server-side blowup beyond proportional reads, no confidentiality impact. The cyclic-structure case is already mitigated by `visited`. Realistic worst case is a sluggish/janky dialog on a pathological share, not a crash.

**Recommendation:**
1. Add a node-count / depth ceiling to `enumerateSharedSubtree` (e.g. cap at a few thousand nodes, stop + return partial with a flag) so a hostile share can't pin the client.
2. In `batchMoveItemsHandler`, hoist a single `getShareKeysFn(shareId)` fetch and pass the result into each move (or have the SDK cache share_keys for the operation), eliminating the N-fetch amplification. Optional but cheap.

### Lens 4 — Error handling / info disclosure: CLEAN (one low nit)

- `SharedMoveDialog.tsx:88` catches enumerate failures and renders a fixed `'Failed to load folder tree'` — no internal ids/paths leaked to the DOM. Good.
- SDK error strings (`'No write key for destination folder'`, `'No read key for destination folder'`, `'Cannot move a folder into itself'`) are generic and contain no key material or ipnsNames. Good.
- `runWrite` (useSharedWriteOps.ts) catches all, suppresses the `write access revoked` message from the user-facing error, and logs via `logger.error`. The full `err` is logged client-side only (the user's own console) — acceptable; not sent server-side. No oracle: the move op validates *both* key records exist before any unwrap, so error timing doesn't distinguish read-vs-write key presence in an attacker-useful way (the actor is the key holder anyway).

### Lens 5 — Over-exposure (projection Pick allowlist): LOW / acceptable

**Location:** `apps/web/src/hooks/shared-folder-projection.ts:38-39` adds `moveInSharedFolder` + `enumerateSharedSubtree` to the `SharedFolderClient` Pick.

**Assessment:** This is the minimal necessary surface — exactly the two methods phase 49 needs, nothing broader. The `Pick<>` allowlist is a typing convenience over the same client instance; it does not grant the UI any capability the UI couldn't already reach via `getSdkClient()` directly (and indeed `SharedMoveDialog` and `useSharedWriteOps` call `getSdkClient().enumerateSharedSubtree/.moveInSharedFolder` directly, bypassing the projection entirely). So the projection widening is cosmetic from a privilege standpoint. No real over-exposure. Not a finding — noting it's clean.

### Lens 6 — State/UX security: 1 functional gap with a security-relevant failure mode

### [LOW] `SelectionActionBar` `onDownload`/`onDelete` wired to no-op `() => {}`

**Location:** `apps/web/src/components/file-browser/SharedFileBrowser.tsx:644-646` (`onDownload={() => {}}` and `onDelete={() => {}}`).

**Issue:** In a write-share multi-select, the action bar renders Download and Delete buttons that silently do nothing. Move is wired; the other two are dead.

**Security-relevant failure mode:** The Delete no-op is the one to flag — a user multi-selects sensitive files in a shared folder, clicks "Delete," sees no error, and may **believe the files were removed/unshared when they were not**. That's a false sense of data deletion (the inverse of the usual "thought it was private" problem). It's a UX/trust bug, not a vulnerability, but it can mislead a user about the disposition of shared data.

**Recommendation:** Either hide/disable the Download and Delete buttons in the action bar until wired, or wire them to the existing single-item `deleteItem`/`downloadSharedFile` handlers in a loop. Do not ship a Delete button that no-ops.

---

### Defense-in-depth nits (not real issues)

- `SharedFolderRow.tsx` `handleDrop` self-drop guard (`parsed.items.some((i) => i.id === item.id)`) trusts the payload `id`s for the *self*-drop check while the actual move routes by selection state — minor inconsistency but harmless, since the SDK self-move throw and the dialog descendant guard are the real backstops.
- `enumerateSharedSubtree` silently skips nodes missing a `folder` read key (client.ts:2451) — correct least-privilege behavior; the picker just won't show unreadable folders. Intentional, good.
- `useFolderNavigation.ts` correctly clones SDK-owned key buffers (`new Uint8Array(state.folderKey)`) to avoid use-after-zero on logout — this is the key-handling lane, out of my scope, but the clone is the right call from a state-integrity view.

---

### Top recommendations (priority order)

1. **Add an authoritative descendant-cycle check in `client.moveInSharedFolder`** (client.ts:2306) so the guard isn't UI-only — closes the crafted-client tree-corruption bypass that can degrade the share for co-recipients.
2. **Bound `enumerateSharedSubtree`** with a node/depth cap and **dedupe the per-item `share_keys` fetch** in `batchMoveItemsHandler` — removes the client-side amplification a hostile share structure could trigger.
3. **Fix the `SelectionActionBar` Delete/Download no-ops** in SharedFileBrowser.tsx:644-646 — at minimum disable the Delete button so users aren't misled about deletion of shared data.

- `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/apps/web/src/components/file-browser/SharedFileBrowser.tsx` (lines 644-646 no-op handlers)
- `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedWriteOps.ts` (`batchMoveItemsHandler` N-fetch amplification)

> AGENT

Finding 2 was a **false positive** — `runWrite` calls `setError(null)` to clear prior errors on entry, so `setError` IS legitimately called once (with `null`) on success. CodeRabbit's `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` doesn't account for that. Reverting to the original intent (no error *string* surfaced) with a clarifying comment.

{
  "file_path": "/tmp/pr-body-49.md",
  "content": "## Summary\n\nPhase 49 lets a **write-permission share recipient move a file between subfolders within a single shared folder**, re-encrypting the file's `FileMetadata` IPNS record from the source subfolder's `folderKey` to the destination subfolder's `folderKey` (mirroring owner `CipherBoxClient.moveItem` and the #507 decrypt-fail-after-move fix) so the file stays decryptable for **owner and recipient** after the move. It also consolidates the duplicated web-side ECIES key-unwrap in `useFolderNavigation` onto the SDK, and brings the shared-view move UX to **parity with the private vault** (batch + drag move).\n\nCloses captured todos `#8` (shared-folder move must re-encrypt file metadata) and `#7` (consolidate the web `useFolderNavigation` key-unwrap into the SDK). Builds on Phase 48's shared-folder ownership (`sharedFolderTree`, `adoptSharedFolderResult`, `sharedFolder:updated`, the key-agnostic `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange`).\n\n**Scope locked:** intra-share moves only (no cross-share, no share↔private-vault); destination picker spans the entire shared subtree; recipient-side capability.\n\n## What's included\n\n- **REQ-1 — SDK shared-subtree enumeration:** `CipherBoxClient.enumerateSharedSubtree` — lazy DFS from the share root, resolving each subfolder's `folderKey` from `share_keys keyType:'folder'` and write-capability from `keyType:'folder-ipns'`; returns `{id, name, ipnsName, writable, parentId}` picker nodes.\n- **REQ-2 — SDK move op + client method:** stateless `moveInSharedFolder` in `share/shared-write.ts` (two explicit src/dest contexts) + `CipherBoxClient.moveInSharedFolder`. Ordering: publish DEST → re-key `FileMetadata` via `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange` (`createVersion:false`, file IPNS key from `share_keys file-ipns`) → publish SOURCE → adopt SOURCE result only → emit. Write-capability checked on both ends; temp keys zeroed in `finally`.\n- **REQ-3 — web single-item move:** `moveItemHandler` in `useSharedWriteOps`, a new shared `MoveDialog` rendering the lazily-loaded shared-subtree picker, `onMove` wired into the folder-view `ContextMenu` (kept off the synthetic list-view), and both SDK methods added to the `SharedFolderClient` projection allowlist.\n- **REQ-4 — `useFolderNavigation` consolidation:** replaced the hand-rolled ECIES unwrap + IPNS-resolve + decrypt with `client.ensureFolderLoaded`, preserving the 3×/2s IPNS-propagation retry and cloning SDK-owned key buffers into `FolderNode` (avoids use-after-zero on `client.destroy()`).\n- **REQ-5 — e2e:** two-account within-share move + decrypt-survival spec (`shared-folder-move.spec.ts`) + page object — asserts content still **decrypts via the TextEditor decrypt-on-read path** for both Bob and Alice after cross-client sync.\n- **REQ-6 — batch + drag parity:** multi-select state + `SelectionActionBar`, a batch handler that loops `moveInSharedFolder` (no SDK batch op — mirrors the private vault), `MoveDialog` `items` prop, and internal drag-and-drop onto `SharedFolderRow`.\n\n## QA performed before this PR\n\n- **/simplify** — reuse + dead-code cleanups (reused `DragItem`/`isExternalFileDrag`, collapsed reset effects).\n- **Security review (crypto + appsec)** — overall risk **LOW**. Fixed: per-iteration `folderKey` zeroing in `enumerateSharedSubtree`; misleading no-op Delete/Download buttons in the shared selection bar. Report in `.planning/security/`.\n- **Correctness hardening** — folder move-cycle guards: SDK throws on move-into-self; the picker disables the moved folder's whole subtree (via `parentId`); drag skips dropping a folder onto itself; batch clears selection only on success.\n- **CodeRabbit CLI** — addressed: drag move now routes by the actually-dragged items (not current selection); `useFolderNavigation` redirects on IPNS-timeout instead of rendering an empty folder; listbox `role=\"option\"`/`aria-selected`; keyboard selection parity.\n\n### Documented security residuals (defense-in-depth, accepted for this PR)\n\n- The **descendant move-cycle** guard is enforced in the UI (dialog `parentId` exclusion + drag self-guard) and the SDK self-move throw, but the SDK op cannot see the full subtree, so a hand-crafted non-UI caller could still create a cycle. The actor must already hold write keys for both folders, the `visited` set prevents any DoS amplification for co-recipients, and such an actor could already vandalise their writable subtree — so an authoritative SDK subtree check is deferred as a follow-up.\n- Batch move re-fetches `share_keys` per item; bounded by user selection — left as a perf follow-up.\n\n## Test status\n\n- SDK unit: `move-in-shared-folder` (13) + `enumerate-shared-subtree` (8) green; full SDK suite passes except 3 pre-existing live-API `integration.test.ts` tests that also fail on `main` without the local docker stack.\n- Web unit: 51/51 (incl. the new `moveItemHandler` case). `tsc -b` + eslint clean across web/sdk; e2e `tsc --noEmit` clean.\n- The REQ-5 e2e is authored + type-checked but **only runs on push to `main` / manual dispatch** (not a PR gate) — it needs the local docker stack. Flagged for live verification.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Commits in this branch are **unsigned** (the 1Password SSH signer was disabled for the autonomous session to avoid wedging). The repo enforces signed commits on PRs — a signed rebase (or admin override) will be needed before merge.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n"

═══ NITPICK 2: shared-move-dialog.page.ts:109-113 ═══
`109-113`: _⚡ Quick win_

**Fail fast in `waitForTreeLoaded` when the dialog enters an error state.**

Line 109-Line 113 can report “loaded” even when subtree loading failed; explicitly checking `loadError` improves diagnostics and reduces flaky downstream failures.

   

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
   async waitForTreeLoaded(options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {
     await this.folderList().waitFor({ state: 'visible', ...options });
     // Allow an extra tick for the loading indicator to disappear
     await this.loadingIndicator().waitFor({ state: 'hidden', timeout: options?.timeout ?? 15_000 });
+    if (await this.loadError().isVisible()) {
+      throw new Error(`SharedMoveDialog failed to load folder tree: ${await this.loadError().textContent()}`);
+    }
   }
```

═══ NITPICK 3: SharedFolderRow.tsx:114-152 ═══
`114-152`: _💤 Low value_

**Type narrowing gap when accessing `item.ipnsName`.**

The `handleDrop` callback accesses `item.ipnsName` at line 149, but TypeScript won't narrow the `FolderChild` union type based on the `isFolder` guard at line 121 because `isFolder` is a derived boolean rather than a type predicate. This could cause a TypeScript error depending on strict settings, since `ipnsName` only exists on `FolderEntry`, not `FilePointer`.




<details>
<summary>🔧 Suggested type-safe access</summary>

```diff
       // Guard: never drop a folder onto itself (one of the dragged items) — that
       // would move it into itself and cycle the tree (mirrors FileListItem).
       if (parsed.items.some((i) => i.id === item.id)) return;

+      // Type guard: onMoveItemTo only set for folders, but narrow for TS
+      if (item.type !== 'folder') return;
+

- Empty items array early-return
- `clearSelection` called only on full success

These edge cases would strengthen confidence in the batch flow.

When running CodeRabbit CLI reviews (`coderabbit review`), use `--agent` instead of `--plain`. The `--agent` mode emits structured findings (severity / file / line / suggested fix) meant for agent consumption; `--plain` is human-oriented prose that is harder to parse reliably.

**Why:** Structured output is far easier to parse and act on programmatically. The CLI itself prints "Detected claude environment. Use `coderabbit review --agent` for structured agent-friendly output." (User instruction, 2026-06-14.)

**How to apply:** Default to `coderabbit review --agent` for all CodeRabbit CLI calls. Keep scoping flags as needed — e.g. `--base-commit <sha>` to bound a review to a single phase's diff when a feature branch stacks multiple phases (the display header still reads "→ main" but the base-commit governs the actual diff).

{
  "file_path": "/Users/myankelev/.claude/projects/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/memory/project-coderabbit-github-review-body-not-threads.md",
  "content": "---\nname: project-coderabbit-github-review-body-not-threads\ndescription: \"CodeRabbit's post-PR GitHub review often bundles nitpicks in the review BODY, not inline threads — /resolve-pr-reviews finds 0 threads\"\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nWhen CodeRabbit reviews a PR on GitHub (the automatic post-PR review, separate from the CLI), nitpick-level findings are frequently bundled into the **review body** of a single `COMMENTED` review (under a `🧹 Nitpick comments (N)` section), NOT posted as inline review threads.\n\n**Why this matters:** The [[resolve-pr-reviews]] skill's `reviewThreads` GraphQL query then returns **0 unresolved threads** even though there are real comments to address — so the skill stops with \"No unresolved review threads\" and misses everything.\n\n**How to apply:**\n\n- Don't trust the thread query alone. Also read the review body:\n  `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N>/reviews --jq '.[] | select(.user.login==\"coderabbitai[bot]\") | .body'`\n  and the issue-comment summary line `Actionable comments posted: K`.\n- The review body groups findings per file under `<summary>path (count)</summary>` blocks; each has a `file:line`, a severity tag (`⚡ Quick win` / `💤 Low value`), a title, a `Proposed fix` diff, and a `🤖 Prompt for AI Agents` block.\n- The CLI (`coderabbit review --agent`, see [[feedback-coderabbit-cli-use-agent-flag]]) emits a different shape — line-delimited JSON `{type:\"finding\", severity, fileName, codegenInstructions, suggestions}`, severities `critical|major|minor`. Parse with node, not jq field-guessing.\n- Since there are no threads, \"resolution\" = apply the valid fixes + push + post a top-level `gh pr comment` summarizing what was addressed/skipped (there's nothing to `resolveReviewThread`).\n- Always verify CodeRabbit suggestions against the live code before applying — they can be wrong (e.g. it suggested `expect(setError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` not realizing `runWrite` calls `setError(null)` to clear; the correct assertion was `.not.toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.any(String))`).\n"
}

19	/**
20	 * Regression: intra-share file move must keep file content decryptable for the
21	 * recipient AND the owner after cross-client sync.
22	 *
23	 * A file's FileMetadata IPNS record is AES-256-GCM sealed with its parent
24	 * folder's folderKey. Moving a file between two subfolders within a shared
25	 * folder tree without re-encrypting the record would make every subsequent
26	 * preview/edit/download fail with "CryptoError: Decryption failed"
27	 * (T-49-03/T-49-14).

46	export function SharedFolderRow({

62	  const isFolder = item.type === 'folder';
63	  const icon = isFolder ? '📁' : '📄';
64	  const date = item.modifiedAt ? new Date(item.modifiedAt).toLocaleDateString() : '--';
65	  const isWrite = permission === 'write';

67	  // Internal drag-over visual state

69	
70	  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
71	  // Drag source -- multi-select-aware (mirrors FileListItem :160-177)
72	  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
73	  const handleDragStart = useCallback(
74	    (e: DragEvent) => {
75	      // If this item is part of a multi-select, payload includes all selected items
76	      const dragItems: DragItem[] =
77	        isSelected && selectedItems.length > 1
78	          ? selectedItems.map((i) => ({ id: i.id, type: i.type }))
79	          : [{ id: item.id, type: item.type }];
80	
81	      const payload: DragPayload = { items: dragItems };
82	      e.dataTransfer.setData('application/json', JSON.stringify(payload));
83	      e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move';
84	    },
85	    [item, isSelected, selectedItems]
86	  );
87	
88	  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	  // Drop target -- folder rows only (mirrors FileListItem :275-317)
90	  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
91	  const handleDragOver = useCallback(
92	    (e: DragEvent) => {
93	      if (!isFolder || !onMoveItemTo) return;
94	      e.preventDefault();
95	      e.stopPropagation();
96	
97	      // Distinguish internal moves from external file uploads
98	      e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = isExternalFileDrag(e.dataTransfer) ? 'copy' : 'move';
99	      setIsDragOver(true);
100	    },
101	    [isFolder, onMoveItemTo]
102	  );
103	
104	  const handleDragLeave = useCallback(

106	      if (!isFolder || !onMoveItemTo) return;
107	      e.preventDefault();
108	      e.stopPropagation();
109	      setIsDragOver(false);
110	    },
111	    [isFolder, onMoveItemTo]
112	  );
113	
114	  const handleDrop = useCallback(
115	    (e: DragEvent) => {
116	      e.preventDefault();
117	      e.stopPropagation();
118	      setIsDragOver(false);
119	
120	      // Only handle drops on folder rows
121	      if (!isFolder || !onMoveItemTo) return;
122	
123	      // Distinguish internal move from external file upload
124	      const jsonData = e.dataTransfer.getData('application/json');
125	
126	      if (!jsonData) {
127	        // External file drop — no handler here; the parent SharedFileBrowser
128	        // handles external drops at the container level
129	        return;
130	      }
131	
132	      // Internal move — parse defensively (T-49-13)
133	      let parsed: DragPayload;

135	        parsed = JSON.parse(jsonData) as DragPayload;
136	        if (!Array.isArray(parsed.items) || parsed.items.length === 0) return;
137	      } catch {
138	        // Invalid JSON — treat as external and let parent handle it
139	        return;
140	      }
141	
142	      // Guard: never drop a folder onto itself (one of the dragged items) — that
143	      // would move it into itself and cycle the tree (mirrors FileListItem).
144	      if (parsed.items.some((i) => i.id === item.id)) return;
145	
146	      // Route through the parent's handleDropOnFolder-equivalent, forwarding the
147	      // dragged items so the parent moves exactly what was dragged. Per-item
148	      // validation (name collision + write-capability) is in the SDK.
149	      onMoveItemTo(item.id, item.ipnsName, parsed.items);
150	    },
151	    [isFolder, item, onMoveItemTo]
152	  );

155	  // Click handler for selection

160	      if (onSelect) {

162	      }
163	    },
164	    [isRenaming, onSelect]
165	  );
166

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const nameText = await rows.nth(i).locator('.file-name').textContent();
      if (nameText) names.push(nameText.trim());
    }
    return names;
  }

> AGENT

Now I see the mechanism for failure 2. I added `onClick` → `handleSelect`, which on a **plain single click** sets `selectedIds` to that one item → `multiSelectActive` becomes true → the `SelectionActionBar` renders *between the toolbar and the file list* (line 643-650), shifting the list down **mid-double-click**. Playwright's `dblclick` dispatches both clicks at fixed coordinates; after the first click's re-render shifts the row, the second click lands elsewhere, so no `dblclick` fires → navigation never happens. Let me confirm how the private vault avoids this (FileListItem click + SelectionActionBar placement).

> AGENT

Both root causes confirmed. The private vault gates its bar on **`selectedIds.size > 1`** (line 205) and renders it *below* the list — so a plain single click (which selects exactly 1) never shows the bar. My shared browser gates on `multiSelectActive = size > 0` (line 149) and renders the bar **above** the list, so the first click of a double-click pops the bar in, shifts the rows down, and the second click misses → `dblclick` never fires → navigation dies. That's failure 2.

Failure 1 is purely my spec asserting the bare folder name when rows render `name/`.

Now I have the complete picture. The established convention for folder-name assertions is slash-tolerant `.includes()` (sharing-workflow, invite-link); my spec used exact `toContain` — that's failure 1. Failure 2 is the single-click→bar→layout-shift regression.

Two targeted fixes:

**Fix 1 (failure 2 — the real regression):** gate the `SelectionActionBar` on `size > 1` (mirroring the private vault), so a plain single click never pops the bar and shifts the list mid-double-click.

> AGENT

Here's where things stand:

## Diagnosis — both web-e2e failures were caused by my PR

**Failure 2 (the real regression — pre-existing `writable-shares.spec.ts` 8.2):**
I added `onClick → select` to `SharedFolderRow` and gated the `SelectionActionBar` on `selectedIds.size > 0`, rendering it **above** the file list. A plain single click — which is also the *first click of a double-click* — selected one item and popped the bar in, shifting the rows down. Playwright's `dblclick` dispatches both clicks at fixed coordinates, so the second click missed the row → the `dblclick` event never fired → folder navigation silently died (breadcrumb stuck on `shared`, 34 retries). The private vault avoids this by gating its bar on **`size > 1`** (`FileBrowser.tsx:205`).

**Failure 1 (my new `shared-folder-move.spec.ts` 3.2):**
`SharedFolderRow` renders folder names with a decorative trailing `/`, so `getFolderItemNames()` returned `"shared-move-dest-…/"`. My spec used exact `toContain(bareName)` — the file matched, the folder didn't. The other specs already use slash-tolerant `.includes()`.

## Fixes pushed (`4bb181995`)
1. **`SharedFileBrowser.tsx`** — gate the batch bar on `selectedIds.size > 1`, mirroring the private vault. Single click still highlights the row; no more mid-double-click layout shift.
2. **`shared-file-browser.page.ts`** — strip the trailing `/` in `getFolderItemNames` so it returns semantic names.

Verified locally: web `tsc -b` ✓, e2e `tsc --noEmit` ✓, eslint ✓, 54/54 web unit tests ✓.

Re-running ci-e2e (**run 27758108928**, in progress) — I'm watching it and will report the result, in particular whether `writable-shares` 8.2 and the `shared-folder-move` spec now pass.

## Summary of Findings

Based on my thorough trace through the CipherBox codebase, here are the answers to your three questions:

---

### **Question 1: Share creation/key distribution — recursive subtree walk?**

**ANSWER: YES, RECURSIVELY at share creation time via `childKeys` parameter, BUT ONLY for pre-existing items at share-time.**

**Evidence:**

         shareId: savedShare.id,
         keyType: ck.keyType,  // 'folder', 'folder-ipns', 'file', 'file-ipns'
         itemId: ck.itemId,

**The critical point:** The `childKeys` are built at share-creation time on the **client-side** (app/web, not shown in your search scope for speed), and they represent a **snapshot of descendants at that moment**. The server accepts them as-is — it does NOT recursively walk the folder tree. This is a zero-knowledge design: the client builds the descendant list, wraps each key for the recipient, and sends them to the API.

---

## **The Crux: Where Does Bob Get the Subfolder IPNS Key?**

**NOT from the parent metadata.** Instead:

1. **At share time**, Alice's client wraps the IPNS key with Bob's public key and sends it as part of `childKeys` → stored in API's `share_keys` table with `keyType: 'folder-ipns'` and `itemId: <subfolder-id>`.

2. **When Bob navigates into the subfolder**, the SDK calls `getShareKeys(shareId)` and finds the row where `keyType === 'folder-ipns' && itemId === targetFolderId`.

3. **Bob unwraps** that `encryptedKey` with his private key to recover the plaintext IPNS private key.

4. **The FolderEntry fields** (`folderKeyEncrypted` and `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` in the parent's metadata) are wrapped with **Alice's** public key (the owner), so Bob cannot decrypt them. They exist so Alice can read her own shared folders and nested structures.

---

**Bottom line for your writability bug:** If a pre-existing subfolder was shared as part of the parent share (included in `childKeys` at share-time), Bob will have a `share_keys` entry for it. If it was created AFTER the parent was shared (Bob created it), the SDK explicitly adds `folder-ipns` keys via `createSharedSubfolder()`. If somehow a subfolder is missing its `folder-ipns` share_keys entry, Bob will downgrade to `permission: 'read'` (line 297 in useSharedNavigationActions.ts).

## Summary of Findings

I have found **conclusive code evidence** that answers your critical question: **Pre-existing nested subfolders in a write share receive ONLY `folder` read-keys, NOT `folder-ipns` write-keys, making them read-only for the recipient even on a write share.**

### 1. The Function That Builds `childKeys` for Folder Share

**File**: `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/apps/web/src/lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts`
**Function**: `collectChildKeys()` (lines 35-120)

This is the core function that recursively traverses all descendant folders and files during share creation. It is called from:
- **Direct share**: `ShareDialog.tsx` line 271-277
- **Invite link share**: `invite.service.ts` line 146-152

### 2. Critical Finding: No `folder-ipns` Keys Are Created for Pre-Existing Descendants

Looking at lines 45-120 of `key-wrapping.ts`, the function iterates through children:

**For FILES** (lines 46-66):
```typescript
if (child.type === 'file') {
  const fp = child as FilePointer;
  const { metadata: fileMeta } = await resolveFileMetadata(fp.fileMetaIpnsName, folderKey);
  const reWrappedFileKey = await reWrapEncryptedKey(...);
  childKeys.push({
    keyType: 'file' as ChildKeyDto['keyType'],  // ← ONLY 'file' keyType
    itemId: fp.id,
    encryptedKey: reWrappedFileKey,
  });
}
```

**For FOLDERS** (lines 68-116):
```typescript
else {
  const folder = child as FolderEntry;
  const folderKeyRewrapped = await reWrapEncryptedKey(
    folder.folderKeyEncrypted,
    ownerPrivateKey,
    targetPubKeyBytes
  );
  childKeys.push({
    keyType: 'folder' as ChildKeyDto['keyType'],  // ← ONLY 'folder' keyType
    itemId: folder.id,
    encryptedKey: folderKeyRewrapped,
  });
  // ... then recurse
  const subKeys = await collectChildKeys(
    metadata.children,
    folderKeyBytes,
    ownerPrivateKey,
    targetPubKeyBytes,
    ...
  );
  childKeys.push(...subKeys);
}
```

**Key Evidence**: The function emits ONLY `'folder'` keyType for descendant folders—never `'folder-ipns'`. There is NO conditional logic checking the permission level ('read' vs 'write'). It does not discriminate between depths or parent-child relationships.

### 3. The Permission Parameter Is Never Passed to `collectChildKeys()`

In `ShareDialog.tsx` (lines 271-277):
```typescript
childKeys = await collectChildKeys(
  metadata.children,
  itemFolderKey,
  ownerPrivateKey,
  recipientPubKeyBytes,
  (wrapped) => setProgress({ current: wrapped, total: 0 })
);
```

The `permission` state (set by the radio buttons on line 93) is **never passed** to `collectChildKeys()`. The function has no visibility into whether the share is 'read' or 'write'.

### 4. For Newly Created Subfolders (Write Shares Only), `folder-ipns` IS Provided

Contrast this with the SDK's `createSharedSubfolder()` function in `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts` (lines 249-335), which is called ONLY during write operations:

```typescript
// 6. Add share_keys for recipient (folder + folder-ipns)
const recipientWrappedFolderKey = await wrapKey(subfolderKey, swCtx.recipientPublicKey);
const recipientWrappedIpnsKey = await wrapKey(keypair.privateKey, swCtx.recipientPublicKey);
try {
  await swCtx.addShareKeysFn(swCtx.shareId, [
    {
      keyType: 'folder',
      itemId: folderId,
      encryptedKey: bytesToHex(recipientWrappedFolderKey),
    },
    {
      keyType: 'folder-ipns',
      itemId: folderId,
      encryptedKey: bytesToHex(recipientWrappedIpnsKey),
    },
  ]);
}
```

**This demonstrates the intended pattern**: Both `'folder'` and `'folder-ipns'` are created for subfolders, but ONLY when they are **newly created** by the write-share recipient.

### 5. How the Recipient Determines Write Access

The SDK test file `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/packages/sdk/src/__tests__/enumerate-shared-subtree.test.ts` (lines 191-206) confirms that write access is determined by the presence of `folder-ipns` keys:

And in the SDK client (lines 2466-2468 of `/packages/sdk/src/client.ts`):
```typescript

```

### 6. How Web Navigation Checks for Write Capability

In `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/apps/web/src/hooks/useSharedNavigationActions.ts` (lines 283-286, 421-424), the same pattern is used:

## Conclusion

**The bug is CONFIRMED**: When a user shares a folder with **READ-WRITE** permission, the `collectChildKeys()` function builds re-wrapped `'folder'` (read) keys for all pre-existing nested subfolders but **does not create `'folder-ipns'` (write) keys for them**. This makes pre-existing nested subfolders read-only for the recipient, even on a write share. Only newly created subfolders (via `createSharedSubfolder()`) receive `folder-ipns` keys automatically, giving them write access to the recipient.

The fix would require either:
1. Passing the `permission` level to `collectChildKeys()` and conditionally emitting `'folder-ipns'` keys when permission='write', OR
2. Modifying `ShareDialog.tsx` to separately emit `'folder-ipns'` keys for all descendant folders when creating a write share.

9	 * in finally blocks.

21	/**
22	 * Collect all descendant keys from a folder for sharing.
23	 * Traverses subfolders depth-first, re-wrapping each file and subfolder key
24	 * for the target public key.
25	 *
26	 * Works for both direct share (recipientPubKey) and invite link (ephemeralPubKey)
27	 * since the target key is parameterized.
28	 *
29	 * @param children - Children of the current folder
30	 * @param folderKey - Decrypted AES key of the current folder (for resolving file metadata)
31	 * @param ownerPrivateKey - Owner's secp256k1 private key for unwrapping ECIES keys
32	 * @param targetPubKeyBytes - Target uncompressed secp256k1 public key (recipient or ephemeral)
33	 * @param onProgress - Callback for progress tracking
34	 */
35	export async function collectChildKeys(
36	  children: FolderChild[],
37	  folderKey: Uint8Array,
38	  ownerPrivateKey: Uint8Array,
39	  targetPubKeyBytes: Uint8Array,
40	  onProgress: (wrapped: number) => void
41	): Promise<ChildKeyDto[]> {
42	  const childKeys: ChildKeyDto[] = [];
43	  let wrapped = 0;
44	
45	  for (const child of children) {
46	    if (child.type === 'file') {
47	      const fp = child as FilePointer;
48	      // Resolve file metadata to get fileKeyEncrypted, then re-wrap for target
49	      try {
50	        const { metadata: fileMeta } = await resolveFileMetadata(fp.fileMetaIpnsName, folderKey);
51	        const reWrappedFileKey = await reWrapEncryptedKey(
52	          fileMeta.fileKeyEncrypted,
53	          ownerPrivateKey,
54	          targetPubKeyBytes
55	        );
56	        childKeys.push({
57	          keyType: 'file' as ChildKeyDto['keyType'],
58	          itemId: fp.id,
59	          encryptedKey: reWrappedFileKey,
60	        });
61	        wrapped++;
62	        onProgress(wrapped);
63	      } catch (err) {
64	        logger.error(`Failed to re-wrap file key for ${fp.name}:`, err);
65	        // Continue with other children
66	      }
67	    } else {
68	      const folder = child as FolderEntry;
69	      // Re-wrap the subfolder's folderKey for the target
70	      try {
71	        const folderKeyRewrapped = await reWrapEncryptedKey(
72	          folder.folderKeyEncrypted,
73	          ownerPrivateKey,
74	          targetPubKeyBytes
75	        );
76	        childKeys.push({
77	          keyType: 'folder' as ChildKeyDto['keyType'],
78	          itemId: folder.id,
79	          encryptedKey: folderKeyRewrapped,
80	        });
81	        wrapped++;
82	        onProgress(wrapped);
83	
84	        // Recurse into subfolder: resolve its metadata and collect its children
85	        const resolved = await resolveIpnsRecord(folder.ipnsName);
86	        if (resolved) {
87	          const folderKeyBytes = await unwrapKey(
88	            hexToBytes(folder.folderKeyEncrypted),
89	            ownerPrivateKey
90	          );
91	          try {
92	            const encryptedBytes = await fetchFromIpfs(resolved.cid);
93	            const encryptedJson = new TextDecoder().decode(encryptedBytes);
94	            const encrypted = JSON.parse(encryptedJson);
95	            const metadata = await decryptFolderMetadata(encrypted, folderKeyBytes);
96	
97	            const subKeys = await collectChildKeys(
98	              metadata.children,
99	              folderKeyBytes,
100	              ownerPrivateKey,
101	              targetPubKeyBytes,
102	              (subWrapped) => {
103	                onProgress(wrapped + subWrapped);
104	              }
105	            );
106	            wrapped += subKeys.length;
107	            childKeys.push(...subKeys);
108	          } finally {
109	            folderKeyBytes.fill(0);
110	          }
111	        }
112	      } catch (err) {
113	        logger.error(`Failed to re-wrap folder key for ${folder.name}:`, err);
114	        // Continue with other children
115	      }
116	    }
117	  }
118	
119	  return childKeys;
120	}

122	/**
123	 * Re-wrap an ECIES-encrypted hex key from owner to target.
124	 *
125	 * Unwraps with ownerPrivateKey, then wraps for targetPubKey.
126	 * Plaintext key is zeroed after use.
127	 */
128	export async function reWrapEncryptedKey(
129	  encryptedKeyHex: string,
130	  ownerPrivateKey: Uint8Array,
131	  targetPubKey: Uint8Array
132	): Promise<string> {
133	  const plainKey = await unwrapKey(hexToBytes(encryptedKeyHex), ownerPrivateKey);
134	  try {
135	    const rewrapped = await wrapKey(plainKey, targetPubKey);
136	    return bytesToHex(rewrapped);
137	  } finally {
138	    plainKey.fill(0);
139	  }
140	}

> AGENT

Confirmed directly from source: `collectChildKeys` emits **only** `'folder'`/`'file'` (read) keys for descendants — no `folder-ipns`/`file-ipns`, and it takes no `permission` param. So a read-write folder share grants the recipient write access **only to the root** and to items they create themselves; every owner-created subfolder/file in the subtree is read-only to them. That's why Bob can't move the owner's file into the owner's subfolder.

This is a genuine cross-layer fork that's your call — it's security-sensitive (it decides whether a write-share hands the recipient IPNS signing keys for the whole subtree) and it expands beyond phase 49's literal plan.

There is no subtree-aware authorization: the only path that lets a non-owner publish is `findActiveWriteShare(userId, ipnsName)` with an exact `ipnsName` match, and write `Share` rows only exist for the explicitly-shared top-level folder. ---

## SECURITY REVIEW COMPLETE

**Files analyzed:** 5 primary + 8 supporting (crypto, IPNS authz, entity/migration, SDK move path)
**Crypto operations reviewed:** ECIES unwrap/re-wrap for `folder`, `file`, `folder-ipns`, `file-ipns` child keys; plaintext-key zeroing lifecycle
**Issues found:** 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium, 2 Low, 3 Info

The cryptographic core of this change is correct and safe. The findings below are about a cross-layer authorization gap (which is a correctness/wasted-distribution concern, not a key-leak) and defense-in-depth hardening.

---

### Assessment of the six requested points

1. **Plaintext key hygiene — PASS.** `reWrapEncryptedKey` (`apps/web/src/lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts:169-181`) unwraps, wraps, and zeros `plainKey` in a `finally`. Every new IPNS path routes through it, so the new `folder-ipns` / `file-ipns` plaintext keys are never held un-zeroed. The recursion's `folderKeyBytes` is zeroed in a `finally` (lines 149-151). The ShareDialog top-level paths (`ipnsPrivKey` 248-258, `fileIpnsPrivKey` 307-325) and invite paths all zero in `finally`. No un-zeroed plaintext key on any path.

2. **ECIES direction — PASS.** Every re-wrap unwraps with `ownerPrivateKey` and wraps with `targetPubKeyBytes` (`key-wrapping.ts:55-59, 73-77, 94-98, 110-114`). `targetPubKeyBytes` is plumbed from `recipientPubKeyBytes` (ShareDialog:275) or `ephemeralKeypair.publicKey` (invite.service:150). No wrap-to-owner, no key confusion.

3. **No over-distribution — PASS (client).** Write keys are emitted only under `permission === 'write'` (`key-wrapping.ts:72, 109`), only for descendants of the explicitly-shared folder (traversal rooted at the shared folder's children), and invites force the literal `'read'` (`invite.service.ts:151-152`). The `'write'` literal cannot reach the invite path.

4. **Legacy files — PASS, with one latent gap (see M-2).** `file-ipns` is correctly guarded on `fp.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` presence (`key-wrapping.ts:72`). `FolderEntry.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` is a required field (`packages/core/src/folder/types.ts:40`), so the unguarded folder-ipns unwrap (line 110-114) is correct for all currently-produced folders.

5. **Validation/DTO soundness — PASS.** `key_type` was widened to `varchar(12)` (migration `1743100000000-WidenShareKeyType.ts`); `'folder-ipns'` is 11 chars. Adding it to `CHILD_KEY_TYPES` is safe: the recipient is the grantee, the owner is the grantor, and downgrade cleanup purges `In(['file-ipns','folder-ipns'])` (`shares.service.ts:431`).

6. **Threat model — see M-1 below.** Distributing descendant IPNS signing keys does NOT let the recipient reach anything outside the shared subtree, because server-side publish authorization is per-`ipnsName` and the recipient only ever receives keys for in-subtree ipnsNames. However, the same per-`ipnsName` check means these keys also do not currently *function* server-side (the gap).

---

### Medium

#### [MEDIUM] Distributed descendant IPNS keys are not honored by server-side publish authorization — the feature is silently non-functional

**Location:** `apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:212-223` ↔ `apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts:440-450` ↔ `packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts:559-591`

**Issue:** The client now distributes a `folder-ipns` key for each descendant subfolder so the recipient can sign IPNS records for those subfolders. But the server authorizes a non-owner publish only via:

```ts
// ipns.service.ts:213
const writeShare = await this.sharesService.findActiveWriteShare(userId, ipnsName);
// shares.service.ts:444 — exact ipnsName equality
where: { recipientId, ipnsName, permission: 'write', encryptedIpnsKey: Not(IsNull()), revokedAt: IsNull() }
```

A write `Share` row exists only for the **top-level** shared folder's `ipnsName` (created in `shares.service.ts:91-106`). No `Share` row carries a descendant subfolder's `ipnsName`. When `moveInSharedFolder` publishes the source and destination subfolders under their own ipnsNames (`shared-write.ts:564, 588`), `findActiveWriteShare(userId, <descendantIpnsName>)` returns `null`, `existing` stays `null`, and the publish falls through to the **create-new-entry path** (`ipns.service.ts:285-302`), creating a *duplicate* FolderIpns owned by the recipient rather than updating the owner's record — or fails downstream. The cross-subfolder move this change is meant to unblock will not actually succeed end-to-end against the real API.

**Impact:** Wasted key distribution (recipient gets `folder-ipns` keys that the server will not let them use), and a latent data-integrity risk: a recipient publishing a descendant ipnsName can mint a recipient-owned `FolderIpns` row that diverges from the owner's record for the same ipnsName (the `getFolderIpns(userId, ...)` lookup at line 206 is per-user, so two rows for one ipnsName can coexist). This is the crux of threat-model point #6 in the inverse direction — not a leak, but an authorization model that the client change has outrun.

**Recommendation:** Make server-side publish authorization subtree-aware. The cleanest approach that matches the existing model is to authorize a descendant publish when the recipient holds a `folder-ipns` / `file-ipns` `ShareKey` row whose `item_id` corresponds to the target ipnsName, under an active write share — i.e., extend `findActiveWriteShare` (or add a sibling) to also match descendant ipnsNames covered by the share's distributed keys. At minimum, confirm with an integration test (live API, not the mocked `shares.service.spec.ts`) that a recipient can publish a descendant subfolder ipnsName. The current unit tests (`shares.service.spec.ts:811`) only prove the recipient may *store* a `folder-ipns` ShareKey row, not that they may *publish* the corresponding ipnsName.

**Suggested test:**

```typescript
describe('write-share descendant publish authorization', () => {
  it('authorizes recipient to publish a descendant subfolder ipnsName covered by the parent write share', async () => {
    // Arrange: owner shares /parent (ipnsP) write; descendant /parent/sub has ipnsS
    //          recipient holds folder-ipns ShareKey for sub
    // Act: recipient publishes ipnsS
    // Assert: server UPDATES owner's FolderIpns(ipnsS), does NOT create a recipient-owned row
  });
  it('rejects recipient publishing an ipnsName NOT in the shared subtree', async () => {
    // Assert: 403/404, no row created
  });
});
```

#### [MEDIUM] Folder metadata validator does not enforce `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` presence — unguarded unwrap could throw on malformed/legacy folder entries

**Location:** `packages/core/src/folder/metadata.ts:60-93` (validation) ↔ `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts:109-114` (unguarded unwrap)

**Issue:** The folder-ipns unwrap is unguarded:

```ts
if (permission === 'write') {
  const reWrappedFolderIpns = await reWrapEncryptedKey(
    folder.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted, // assumed present
    ownerPrivateKey,
    targetPubKeyBytes
  );
```

This relies on `FolderEntry.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` always being present. The TypeScript type marks it required (`folder/types.ts:40`), but the runtime validator in `decryptFolderMetadata` validates `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` **only for `file` entries** (lines 72-92) — there is no presence/format check for `folder` entries. So a folder entry from a future/old metadata version, or a corrupted record, with a missing or short `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` would pass validation, reach the unguarded unwrap, and `hexToBytes(undefined)` / a too-short ciphertext would throw `KEY_UNWRAPPING_FAILED`. Because that throw is inside the per-child `try/catch` (lines 93-156), the failure is swallowed and the subfolder plus **its entire subtree** is silently dropped from the share (the recipient gets a folder they can read into but with missing descendant keys), rather than failing loudly.

**Impact:** Low likelihood today (all current folders carry the key), but it is a silent-partial-share failure mode with no signal to the user. The type-vs-runtime mismatch is exactly the kind of assumption that breaks on a metadata-version bump.

**Recommendation:** Either (a) add a presence/format check for `folder` entries' `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` in `metadata.ts` mirroring the file branch, or (b) guard the folder-ipns unwrap on presence like the file path does — `if (permission === 'write' && folder.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted)` — and treat a missing key as "this subtree stays read-only," consistent with the documented legacy-file behavior. Option (b) is the smaller, safer change and matches the existing pattern at line 72.

---

### Low

#### [LOW] Redundant double-wrap of the file IPNS key in the single-file write-share path

**Location:** `apps/web/src/components/file-browser/ShareDialog.tsx:307-326`

**Issue:** In the single-file write path, `fileIpnsPrivKey` is wrapped twice for the same recipient: once into `encryptedIpnsKeyHex` (line 313-314) and again into `recipientWrappedIpnsKey` for the `file-ipns` child key (line 317). ECIES is non-deterministic (fresh ephemeral key per wrap), so these are two different ciphertexts of the same plaintext. Functionally harmless and the plaintext is zeroed once in `finally` (line 324), but it is a redundant crypto op and a minor code smell — the second `wrapKey` could reuse the first result's plaintext-equivalence intent, or the two destinations could share one wrap.

**Impact:** None to security. Two ciphertexts of the same key for the same recipient is not a weakness (no nonce-reuse — each ECIES wrap uses an independent ephemeral key).

**Recommendation:** Optional cleanup — wrap once, reuse the hex for both `encryptedIpnsKey` and the `file-ipns` child key, or document why both fields carry the same key.

#### [LOW] Progress counter `wrapped` can momentarily exceed the eventual total during recursion

**Location:** `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts:142-147`

**Issue:** Each write-share descendant now emits two `onProgress` ticks (read key + ipns key), and the recursion adds `subKeys.length` post-hoc (line 147) while the inner callback already advanced `wrapped + subWrapped` (line 144). This is purely a UI counter (`total: 0` is passed throughout, so there's no bar to overflow). No correctness impact on keys.

**Impact:** Cosmetic only.

**Recommendation:** None required; flag only if the progress UI is later given a real total.

---

### Info

- **Self-consistency of the DTO description string:** `create-share.dto.ts:17` still says "Type of key: file, folder, or file-ipns" while the enum now includes `folder-ipns`. Doc-only drift; the `enum: [...CHILD_KEY_TYPES]` is correct. Same stale text in `claim-invite.dto.ts:18` and `create-invite.dto.ts:18`.
- **Downgrade cleanup is correct and atomic:** `shares.service.ts:427-432` deletes both `file-ipns` and `folder-ipns` ShareKeys plus nulls `encryptedIpnsKey` in one transaction. Combined with `findActiveWriteShare`'s `encryptedIpnsKey: Not(IsNull())` predicate, a downgraded recipient loses both the root IPNS key and all distributed descendant signing keys. Revocation/forge surface is properly bounded.
- **Replay/forge specific to IPNS keys vs AES keys:** Granting a `folder-ipns` key lets the recipient produce *new* signed IPNS records (monotonic sequence), not just read — strictly more power than an AES folder key. That is the intended semantics of a write share and is correctly gated on `permission === 'write'`. The residual concern is purely M-1 (server doesn't yet scope this per-subtree), not the key distribution itself.

---

### Recommendations (priority order)

1. **Resolve M-1 before relying on this for cross-subfolder moves.** The client distributes descendant IPNS keys, but `ipns.service.ts:212-223` will not authorize the recipient to publish descendant ipnsNames, and the fall-through create path can fork the IPNS record. Add subtree-aware publish authorization and a live-API integration test (the existing `shares.service.spec.ts` mocks prove storage, not publish).
2. **Guard the folder-ipns unwrap (M-2)** with `&& folder.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted`, or add folder-entry validation in `metadata.ts`, to avoid silently dropping a subtree from a share on malformed/future metadata.
3. **Sync the three DTO description strings** to mention `folder-ipns` (Info), and optionally de-duplicate the file-ipns double-wrap (L-1).

---

### Overall risk verdict: **MEDIUM** for merging

The cryptography is sound — correct ECIES direction, complete plaintext-key zeroing on all paths including errors, no over-distribution, invites correctly forced to read-only, and clean downgrade revocation. There is **no key-leak or confidentiality risk** in this change.

The MEDIUM verdict is driven by **M-1**: this is a cross-layer change where the client (and DTO/entity) now distribute descendant IPNS signing keys, but the server's per-`ipnsName` publish authorization (`findActiveWriteShare`) has not been extended to honor them. As written, the very feature this unblocks — moving files between owner-created subfolders in a shared folder — will not complete end-to-end and risks forking the descendant IPNS records into recipient-owned duplicate rows. If the server-side authorization counterpart lands in the same PR (or already exists in a path I should be pointed to), this drops to LOW. Merging the client-only half in isolation is not recommended.

Verified. `findActiveWriteShare` is an exact-`ipnsName` match, and `getCoveringShares` is a **client-side** callback (for re-wrapping on upload), not a server authorization path. So there is no server mechanism today to authorize a recipient publishing a *descendant* ipnsName — the server can't even map a descendant ipnsName back to the share (share_keys store the item UUID, not the ipnsName).

This materially changes the picture from when you chose "fix key distribution." Here's the full situation:

## The feature needs three layers; I've done one

| Layer | Status |
|---|---|
| **Client** distributes descendant write keys (`folder-ipns`/`file-ipns`) | ✅ done (this session) |
| **Move op** re-keys FileMetadata across folderKeys | ✅ done (phase 49) |
| **Server** authorizes a recipient to *publish* a descendant ipnsName | ❌ **missing (M-1)** |

Without the server piece, Bob can now *sign* Alice's subfolder record but the server rejects the update and **forks a duplicate recipient-owned IPNS record** (`ipns.service.ts:212-223` → create-new path at `:287`). The security review rated the crypto **sound** (correct ECIES direction, full key-zeroing, no over-distribution, invites stay read-only) but flagged M-1 as a **MEDIUM blocker**: "merging the client-only half in isolation is not recommended."

The server fix is real work: the server has no descendant-ipnsName → share link, so it needs the descendant's ipnsName persisted on the write child-keys + **a DB migration** + subtree-aware publish authorization — security-critical (must never authorize an out-of-subtree publish) and hard to reverse. That's a phase's worth of work, not a tweak.

Notably: moving a file the recipient **owns** (uploaded) into a subfolder the recipient **created** works end-to-end *today* with zero key/server changes (that's what the green `writable-shares` 8.x tests exercise) — because the recipient owns those IPNS records.

 * REQ-4 / Phase-14 finding M1: encrypt share/invite display names at rest.

140	  /**
141	   * Batch publish multiple IPNS records with concurrency-limited processing.
142	   * Supports partial success: individual record failures do not fail the batch.
143	   * Processes up to 10 records concurrently.
144	   */
145	  async publishBatch(
146	    userId: string,
147	    dto: BatchPublishIpnsDto
148	  ): Promise<BatchPublishIpnsResponseDto> {
149	    const results: PublishIpnsResponseDto[] = [];
150	    let totalSucceeded = 0;
151	    let totalFailed = 0;
152	
153	    const CONCURRENCY = 10;
154	
155	    // Process records in batches of CONCURRENCY, delegating to publishRecord
156	    for (let i = 0; i < dto.records.length; i += CONCURRENCY) {
157	      const batch = dto.records.slice(i, i + CONCURRENCY);
158	
159	      const settled = await Promise.allSettled(
160	        batch.map((entry) => this.publishRecord(userId, entry, entry.recordType ?? 'folder'))
161	      );
162	
163	      for (let j = 0; j < settled.length; j++) {
164	        const result = settled[j];
165	        if (result.status === 'fulfilled') {
166	          results.push(result.value);
167	          totalSucceeded++;
168	        } else {
169	          const reason = result.reason;
170	          // If any record (especially a folder record) has a conflict, fail the entire batch
171	          if (reason instanceof ConflictException) {
172	            throw reason;
173	          }
174	          const ipnsName = batch[j]?.ipnsName ?? 'unknown';
175	          this.logger.warn(
176	            `Batch publish failed for ${ipnsName}: ${reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : String(reason)}`
177	          );
178	          results.push({
179	            success: false,
180	            ipnsName,
181	            sequenceNumber: '0',
182	          });
183	          totalFailed++;
184	        }
185	      }
186	    }
187	
188	    return { results, totalSucceeded, totalFailed };
189	  }

Good question — and it gets at something real. Short answer: **cryptographically you're right, but CipherBox doesn't resolve IPNS purely over the DHT, so key-possession alone isn't enough.** Let me explain what I found in the code, because it changes nothing about *your* mental model of IPNS — it's about CipherBox's relay architecture.

## Why the server is in the loop

**1. CipherBox relays IPNS through its own DB, and that DB is the source of truth for resolution.**
A publish writes the signed record to the `folder_ipns` table *synchronously first*, then fire-and-forgets to the DHT (`ipns.service.ts:86-107` — "Save to DB first so resolve always has a fallback"). Resolution *prefers* that DB row because the DHT is slow (~10-30s) and serves stale records (`resolveRecord` always checks the DB cache, `:416-420`). So whoever updates the DB row controls what everyone resolves — the DHT record Bob signs is almost a side-show.

**2. That DB table is keyed per-user.** `@Unique(['userId', 'ipnsName'])` (`folder-ipns.entity.ts:15`). Alice's subfolder record is *Alice's row*. When Bob publishes that same ipnsName, `upsertFolderIpns` looks it up by `(userId=Bob, ipnsName)` (`:206`), finds nothing, and — with no authorization — **forks a second, Bob-owned row** (`:287`). Now two rows exist for one ipnsName, and `resolveRecord` does `findOne({ where: { ipnsName } })` with no user filter and no ordering (`:418-420`) → it returns an *arbitrary* one. Alice keeps seeing her stale row; the move is invisible to her.

**3. The TEE would revert Bob even on the DHT.** Every 6h the TEE republishes the **owner's enrolled** row to the DHT. Bob's update lives in a different (non-enrolled) row, so the TEE rebroadcasts Alice's *stale* record and overwrites Bob's DHT publish. So even the pure-DHT path isn't durable for him.

So Bob's validly-signed record has to land **in Alice's canonical/enrolled row** — and "may Bob write Alice's row?" is necessarily a server authorization decision. The server isn't re-deriving or needing the keys; it's deciding which DB row a valid record updates. This already happens for the **top-level** shared folder (`findActiveWriteShare`, `:213`); it's just missing for descendant subfolders (the M-1 gap).

## There's a second reason, and it's why I'd keep the server approach: **revocation**

CipherBox lets Alice revoke Bob's write access *without rotating IPNS keys* — on downgrade it deletes Bob's `folder-ipns`/`file-ipns` rows and nulls `encryptedIpnsKey` (`shares.service.ts:431`), and the server simply stops authorizing his publishes. If we instead authorized **purely by key possession** (your intuition — "he has the key, let him publish"), then once Bob holds the IPNS private key he could update *forever*, and revocation would require rotating the subfolder's IPNS key and re-sharing. The server-side share check is what makes write access **revocable**.

That's exactly why my approach is the minimal consistent extension of what already exists: persist each write descendant's ipnsName on its `share_keys` row, and authorize a descendant publish iff Bob holds a live write-share key for that ipnsName — same revocable model the top-level share already uses.

## IPNS Architecture Migration: Server-side Signature Verification & DB Key Change

### SECTION 1: Server-side IPNS Record Signature Verification (CRITICAL)

**VERDICT: YES — Readily available via the `ipns` npm package**

#### Verification Function Details

**Location & Import:**
- **Package:** `ipns@10.1.3` (already in `/packages/core/package.json` dependencies)
- **Module path:** `ipns/validator`
- **Function signature:**
```typescript
export declare function validate(publicKey: PublicKey, marshalledRecord: Uint8Array): Promise<void>;
```
- **Semantics:** Validates the SignatureV2 (Ed25519 signature) of a marshaled IPNS record against a given public key. Throws an error if validation fails; returns void if valid.

**Secondary validator for routing-key scenarios:**
```typescript
export declare function ipnsValidator(routingKey: Uint8Array, marshalledRecord: Uint8Array): Promise<void>;
```

**How to use in the API:**

1. **Extract the public key from the incoming record:**
   - Current code already parses it via `/apps/api/src/ipns/ipns-record-parser.ts:54–66` (function `extractEd25519PubKey`), extracting the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key from the protobuf-wrapped libp2p format.
   - Or use the `ipns` package's built-in: `extractPublicKeyFromIPNSRecord(record)` (exported from `ipns/utils`).

2. **Call validate() in publishRecord():**
   - Location: `/apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:47–138` (publishRecord method)
   - Current code only derives and compares publicKey ↔ ipnsName at lines 79–83 (via `deriveIpnsName`).
   - **Add after line 84:**
   ```typescript
   // Verify the Ed25519 SignatureV2 over the IPNS record data
   try {
     const libp2pPublicKey = privateKeyFromRaw(publicKeyBytes); // from @libp2p/crypto/keys
     await validate(libp2pPublicKey, recordBytes);
   } catch (error) {
     throw new BadRequestException('IPNS record signature verification failed');
   }
   ```

**Why this works:**
- The `ipns` npm package (v10.1.3) implements full IPFS IPNS record validation per the IPNS spec, including SignatureV2 verification against Ed25519 keys.
- Both V1 (RSA-legacy) and V2 (Ed25519) signatures are validated.
- The marshalled protobuf record (already received in `dto.record`) contains the `signatureV2` (field 8) and `data` (field 9) fields, which the validator uses.
